knownIssues.title: Process App deployment fails with 'snapshot already exists' error
knownIssues.content: A snapshot with the same name already exists in the Process Center or Process Server. Solution: in Process Designer, increment the snapshot version before creating a new one, or delete the old snapshot from the Process Admin Console (PAC) under Installed Apps > select app > Snapshots > Delete.

knownIssues.title: BAW process app shows 'Team not found' after migration
knownIssues.content: The team references in the process are bound to user group names that differ between environments. Solution: in Process Designer, open Manage > Teams, verify that all team assignments point to groups that exist in the target Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) or user registry; use the 'Process App Settings > Team Bindings' screen to remap.

knownIssues.title: Heritage Process App throws 'CWLLG2007E: The coach could not be found' at runtime
knownIssues.content: The coach view reference in the process is broken, usually after renaming a view artifact. Solution: in Process Designer, search for the broken coach reference via 'Find > Usage', relink to the correct coach view, and redeploy the snapshot.

knownIssues.title: Deploy to Process Server returns HTTP 500 from the REST API
knownIssues.content: The Process Server may have a deployment lock from a stuck previous operation. Solution: in PAC > Servers, check the server status for any pending operations; if stuck, restart the BAW JVM from the WebSphere admin console (Servers > Application Servers > server1 > Restart) and retry the deployment.

knownIssues.title: Process Designer shows blank canvas after opening a complex process
knownIssues.content: The browser has run out of rendering memory for a large BPMN diagram. Solution: use Mozilla Firefox with hardware acceleration enabled; alternatively, open the process in a different browser or reduce diagram complexity by converting subprocess groups.

knownIssues.title: Toolkit dependency version mismatch causes 'incompatible snapshot' warning
knownIssues.content: The process app references a toolkit version that is not installed on the target server. Solution: in Process Designer, open Toolkits, check the dependency version, and either update to the version installed on the server or install the required toolkit version via PAC > Toolkits > Import.

knownIssues.title: BAW workflow instance stuck in 'Running' state with no active tasks
knownIssues.content: An unhandled Java exception or intermediate event caused the instance to stall. Solution: in PAC > Process Instances, locate the instance, open its execution path, and use 'Move token' to advance the token past the stuck node; alternatively, use the BPD debugger to inspect the variable state.

knownIssues.title: Process App installation fails on WAS cluster: 'application already exists'
knownIssues.content: The previous installation left a partially deployed artifact in the WebSphere cell. Solution: remove the orphaned application from WAS Admin Console > Applications > WebSphere Enterprise Applications, then redeploy; confirm with 'wsadmin -lang jython' that the application is fully uninstalled before the next attempt.

knownIssues.title: JavaScript in a service flow throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'
knownIssues.content: A process variable expected to be populated by the previous task is null at the current node. Solution: add a null check at the start of the script (if (tw.local.myVar != null)) and log the variable state with tw.system.currentDate to trace the flow; verify that the previous task output mapping is correctly set.

knownIssues.title: 'Snapshot not found' error when connecting Process Designer to Process Center
knownIssues.content: The Process Center URL or credentials changed after the designer was last connected. Solution: in Process Designer, go to Preferences > IBM BPM > Process Center and update the server URL and credentials; if the server certificate changed, import the new certificate into the JVM trust store.

knownIssues.title: BAW process app upgrade removes custom SCA module bindings
knownIssues.content: When upgrading a snapshot in a clustered environment, the SCA module bindings are reset to defaults. Solution: before upgrading, export the SCA module bindings via wsadmin, perform the upgrade, then re-import the bindings; document all custom bindings in a runbook to avoid post-upgrade downtime.

knownIssues.title: Process Designer crashes when saving large BPMN with many swimlanes
knownIssues.content: Process Designer client has a memory ceiling that is exceeded by complex diagrams. Solution: in the eclipse.ini file of the designer installation, increase -Xmx to at least 2048m and -XX:MaxPermSize to 512m; close unused tabs before saving large processes.

knownIssues.title: Task does not appear in the user's task list in Process Portal
knownIssues.content: The task is assigned to a team, but the user is not a member of that team in the current environment. Solution: check team membership in PAC > User Management > Teams; alternatively verify via REST API: GET /rest/bpm/wle/v1/team?teamName=TeamName and confirm the user appears in the returned member list.

knownIssues.title: Task list in Process Portal loads slowly (>10 seconds)
knownIssues.content: The task query is hitting an unindexed column in the BPMDB. Solution: run EXPLAIN PLAN on the LSW_TASK table queries from the BAW slow query log; add indexes on TASKID, STATUS, and ASSIGNED_TO_USER columns; also check that the database statistics are up to date.

knownIssues.title: User sees 'You are not authorized to access this task' after being reassigned
knownIssues.content: The new assignee does not have the correct lane permission in the process. Solution: in Process Designer, open the BPD, select the lane containing the task, and verify that the team in the 'Assigned To' field includes the new user; redeploy the snapshot after correcting the assignment.

knownIssues.title: Bulk task reassignment via REST API returns 403 Forbidden
knownIssues.content: The calling service account does not have the 'tw_admins' role or task administration rights. Solution: in PAC > User Management, add the service account to the tw_admins group; for least-privilege, create a custom role with only the reassign permission using the BPM Authorization API.

knownIssues.title: Delegated tasks disappear from the delegate's task list after 24 hours
knownIssues.content: The delegation is configured with a time-limited rule that expires. Solution: in PAC > User Management > Delegation, review the delegation rule expiry settings; if the rule should be permanent, set the end date to 'No end date' and save.

knownIssues.title: 'Claiming' a task returns 'Task already claimed by another user'
knownIssues.content: Two users submitted the claim request at the same time, causing a race condition. Solution: this is expected behavior in BAW; implement optimistic locking by catching the TaskAlreadyClaimedException in the coach flow and redirecting the second user back to the task list with a friendly message.

knownIssues.title: Group-assigned tasks not visible to AD group members after LDAP sync
knownIssues.content: The LDAP sync job has not propagated the new AD group membership to the BPM user registry. Solution: force a sync via PAC > User Management > Synchronize Now; check the WAS SystemOut.log for LDAP sync errors; verify that the LDAP federated repository in WAS security settings points to the correct LDAP base DN.

knownIssues.title: Task due date is shown incorrectly in Process Portal (off by 2-3 hours)
knownIssues.content: The server JVM timezone does not match the user's browser timezone. Solution: set the JVM timezone explicitly in the server startup script (-Duser.timezone=Europe/Istanbul); for existing tasks, the due dates can be corrected via the BAW REST PATCH /task endpoint.

knownIssues.title: Completing a task with a JavaScript validation error leaves it in a limbo state
knownIssues.content: The coach JavaScript validation threw an exception after the server acknowledged the completion, causing a split-brain state. Solution: in PAC > Process Instances, find the instance and use 'Force Complete' on the stuck task; review and fix the coach JS validation logic to ensure exceptions are caught gracefully.

knownIssues.title: User receives duplicate task notifications for the same task
knownIssues.content: The user belongs to multiple teams that are all assigned to the same lane, causing the notification engine to fire multiple times. Solution: in Process Designer, assign each lane to a single, specific team; for tasks that should go to multiple teams, use the 'Route Task' service to assign explicitly at runtime.

knownIssues.title: REST external service returns 'SSL handshake failed' in BAW
knownIssues.content: The external service certificate is not trusted by the BAW JVM trust store. Solution: export the service's SSL certificate (openssl s_client -connect host:443), then import it into the WAS JVM trust store via 'ikeyman' tool or WAS Admin Console > Security > SSL certificate and key management > Key stores and certificates > NodeDefaultTrustStore > Signer certificates > Retrieve from port.

knownIssues.title: HTTP connector in service flow returns 'Connection refused' to internal REST API
knownIssues.content: The target URL uses an internal hostname that does not resolve from the BAW server's network segment. Solution: verify DNS resolution from the BAW server with 'nslookup internal-api.corp.local'; add a host entry or configure the HTTP connector to use the IP address; check that firewall rules allow the outbound port.

knownIssues.title: Web Service call in BAW returns SOAP fault 'Invalid Security Token'
knownIssues.content: The WS-Security UsernameToken timestamp has drifted beyond the allowed tolerance. Solution: synchronize the BAW server clock with NTP (w32tm /resync on Windows, ntpdate on Linux); if the issue recurs, increase the timestamp tolerance on the SOAP service side.

knownIssues.title: UCA (Undercover Agent) does not trigger on REST event
knownIssues.content: The event message is being dropped because the correlation condition does not match any running instance. Solution: enable UCA debug logging in WAS via 'com.lombardisoftware.*=FINEST'; verify that the event message body matches the expected correlation variable; use the BAW REST API to manually fire the event for testing.

knownIssues.title: Outbound HTTP integration returns 'Read timeout' after exactly 30 seconds
knownIssues.content: The default HTTP socket read timeout in BAW is 30 seconds. Solution: in BAW system settings (99Local.xml or via the Process Admin Console > Settings), increase the 'externalCallTimeout' or the specific connector timeout; for long-running external operations, consider using an async callback pattern.

knownIssues.title: JSON parse error when consuming REST API response with Turkish characters
knownIssues.content: The HTTP connector is not setting the response charset to UTF-8 before parsing. Solution: in the BAW HTTP connector configuration, set the 'Response content type' to 'application/json;charset=UTF-8'; if the external API returns ISO-8859-9, add a conversion step using the BAW JavaScript tw.system.encoding API.

knownIssues.title: REST service created via Service Designer returns 404 when called from an external system
knownIssues.content: The service is exposed under a snapshot that is not set as the default. Solution: in PAC > Installed Apps, select the process app snapshot, and set it as the default snapshot; verify the exposed URL matches the calling client's URL pattern (include /rest/bpm/wle/v1/... prefix).

knownIssues.title: Database query in an Integration Service returns 'ORA-01000: maximum open cursors exceeded'
knownIssues.content: The JDBC data source connection pool is leaking cursors due to unclosed ResultSets. Solution: wrap all JDBC operations in try-finally blocks to ensure ResultSets and Statements are closed; check the WAS JDBC data source 'Connection pool' settings and enable 'Purge policy: Failing connection only'; consider upgrading to the JAX-RS REST pattern instead of raw JDBC.

knownIssues.title: BAW server CPU spikes to 100% every hour on the hour
knownIssues.content: A scheduled cleanup job or timer UCA is running expensive queries at the top of each hour. Solution: check PAC > System Lanes > Scheduled Tasks for any hourly timers; review the WAS server performance monitor (PMI) thread dump at peak time to identify the hot method; consider staggering scheduled jobs with random offsets.

knownIssues.title: BPMDB tablespace growing rapidly, disk nearly full
knownIssues.content: BAW process instance history is not being purged. Solution: enable the BAW cleanup service via PAC > Admin > Manage Cleanup (set retention days for completed instances); for immediate relief, run the BAW database cleanup script provided in the IBM documentation; schedule weekly automated cleanup to prevent recurrence.

knownIssues.title: Process Portal dashboard widgets take 45+ seconds to load
knownIssues.content: The dashboard queries are running full table scans on the LSW_TASK and LSW_BPD_INSTANCE tables. Solution: collect EXPLAIN PLAN for the dashboard queries from the BAW SQL trace log; add composite indexes on (STATUS, DUE_DATE, ASSIGNED_TO_DEPT); also verify that the BAW Elasticsearch index is active and populated for search-backed widgets.

knownIssues.title: BAW cluster node reports 'OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space' under load
knownIssues.content: The JVM heap is exhausted during peak process load. Solution: increase the JVM -Xmx from 2g to 4g in the application server profile; enable GC logging (-Xloggc) to identify memory leak patterns; check for large process variable data (e.g., base64-encoded documents stored as strings) that should be externalized to FileNet.

knownIssues.title: Dashboards show stale data - tracking group counts not updating
knownIssues.content: The BAW tracking group update is failing silently due to a locked row in the tracking tables. Solution: check the BAW SystemOut.log for 'tracking group update failed'; run 'UNLOCK TABLES' on the LSW_TRACKED_OBJECT table in BPMDB; restart the tracking agent via PAC > System Lanes > Tracking.

knownIssues.title: Document upload fails with 'ObjectStore not found' error in ACCE
knownIssues.content: The Object Store name in the URL or connection profile does not match the deployed Object Store. Solution: in ACCE (Admin Console for Content Engine), verify the Object Store symbolic name under Domain > Object Stores; update the client application connection string to use the exact symbolic name including case sensitivity.

knownIssues.title: Large file upload (>500MB) times out in the FileNet web client
knownIssues.content: The WebSphere session timeout and Content Engine chunked upload timeout are both set too low. Solution: increase 'com.ibm.CONTENTENGINE.upload.chunkedThresholdSize' in ce-bootstrap.properties; in WAS, extend the HTTP session timeout; consider using the CMIS protocol for large uploads as it supports multi-part upload natively.

knownIssues.title: Document version is not incremented after check-in
knownIssues.content: The document was checked in with the 'Same version' option selected instead of 'Minor' or 'Major'. Solution: instruct users to always select the correct version increment type at check-in; if a document was accidentally left at the same version, use ACCE to manually set the version label.

knownIssues.title: 'FNRCE0061E: The document cannot be checked out' error
knownIssues.content: The document is already checked out by another user. Solution: in ACCE, navigate to the document, open its properties, and under 'Reservation' use 'Cancel Checkout' (requires administrative rights); the previously checked-out copy is lost and must be re-uploaded.

knownIssues.title: Documents uploaded via API missing metadata fields
knownIssues.content: The API call is not setting all required property values defined in the document class. Solution: review the document class definition in ACCE for required properties (those marked 'Not Nullable'); update the API client to populate all required properties in the PropertiesType list; validate with a CMIS browser test.

knownIssues.title: Full-text search returns no results for recently uploaded documents
knownIssues.content: The Content Engine full-text indexer queue is backed up or the indexing service is stopped. Solution: check the indexing status in ACCE > Domain > Content Engine Services > Index; review the CBR (Content-Based Retrieval) sweep queue size; restart the CBR dispatcher if the queue is not moving.

knownIssues.title: FileNet folder structure cannot be navigated after permission change
knownIssues.content: The 'Browse' access right was removed from an intermediate folder, breaking navigation for users who have access to subfolders. Solution: in ACCE, open the intermediate folder's properties > Permissions, and grant 'Browse' to the affected group; maintain a permission audit log to prevent similar issues.

knownIssues.title: 'FNRCA0060E: The annotation cannot be created' error in Daeja ViewONE
knownIssues.content: The annotation object store is not configured or the user does not have 'Create' rights on the annotation class. Solution: verify annotation storage configuration in ACCE > Object Store > Other Properties > Annotation Store; grant 'Major Version' and 'Create Instance' rights on the Annotation class to the user's group.

knownIssues.title: Document retention policy incorrectly marks active documents for deletion
knownIssues.content: The retention trigger event is set to 'Create Date' instead of 'Date Last Modified'. Solution: in ACCE, navigate to the document class > Retention Policy, and change the trigger to the appropriate event (usually 'Date Last Modified' or a custom disposition date property); run a test on a small subset before applying broadly.

knownIssues.title: Content Engine reports 'fixedContent area full' error
knownIssues.content: The file storage area has reached its configured maximum size. Solution: add a new file storage area in ACCE > Object Store > File Storage Areas > New; the Content Engine will automatically distribute new content to the new area; consider migrating older content to archival storage using IS Records Manager.

knownIssues.title: Bulk document import via eXeLoader fails with checksum mismatch
knownIssues.content: The source file was modified after the checksum was calculated, or the file was corrupted during transfer. Solution: re-generate the checksum file for the batch using the eXeLoader utility; ensure file transfers use binary mode, not text mode, to avoid line-ending conversions that corrupt binary documents.

knownIssues.title: User gets 'Access denied' when opening a document they should see
knownIssues.content: The document-level permission is overriding the folder-level permission. Solution: in ACCE, check the document's individual security policy and inherited permissions separately; verify that the user's group is in the document's Access Control List (ACL) with at least 'View Content' and 'Read Properties' rights.

knownIssues.title: LDAP users cannot log in to FileNet Application Engine after AD group change
knownIssues.content: The LDAP cache in the Content Engine has not been updated with the new AD group membership. Solution: restart the Content Engine Application Server to force an LDAP cache flush; or use the CE Security Cache flush API: GET /wsi/FNCEWS40MTOM/?action=refreshCache.

knownIssues.title: Service account password change breaks all FileNet integrations
knownIssues.content: The GCD (Global Configuration Data) and LDAP bind credentials are stored with the old password. Solution: update the LDAP bind account password in WAS > Security > Global security > Federated repositories; update the GCD user credentials in ACCE > Domain > Credentials; restart the Content Engine application server.

knownIssues.title: Role-based access via Roles object store is not working as expected
knownIssues.content: The role membership was added to a Role directly, but the role was not then assigned to the ACL of the target object class. Solution: in ACCE, navigate to the Role object, verify its members, then open the target Object Class > Default Instance Security and add the Role to the ACL with the appropriate rights.

knownIssues.title: Security policy propagation to existing documents is incomplete
knownIssues.content: When a new security policy is applied, only new documents inherit it; existing documents are unaffected. Solution: use the IBM Content Navigator Administration Console to run a batch security update job; for very large repositories, use the CE Java API to iterate and apply the new policy in off-hours batches.

knownIssues.title: External user invited to a shared folder cannot view documents
knownIssues.content: External user accounts created via the guest mechanism do not have the 'Authenticated Users' group membership required by the default security policy. Solution: create a dedicated external user group, add the external user to it, and add this group to the relevant security policies with 'Read' access; do not add external users to internal groups.

knownIssues.title: ICN (IBM Content Navigator) workflow task not appearing in inbox
knownIssues.content: The workflow roster configuration in the Process Engine does not match the user's PE group membership. Solution: in Process Engine Configuration Manager, verify the roster for the workflow step and confirm the user's PE group has been synchronized from LDAP; use PE Admin to manually add the user to the correct PE group as a temporary fix.

knownIssues.title: Document approval workflow stuck at 'Pending' with no active step
knownIssues.content: A step notification email failed to send, leaving the workflow waiting for a user response that was never received. Solution: in ICN > Workflow inbox, use the 'Reassign' function to move the stuck step to another user or group; check the SMTP relay configuration in the workflow definition to prevent recurrence.

knownIssues.title: FileNet workflow step returns 'Deadline exceeded' immediately after assignment
knownIssues.content: The step deadline is set to a negative or zero value due to a miscalculation in the workflow definition. Solution: open the workflow definition in the Workflow Designer, navigate to the problematic step, and set a realistic deadline (e.g., 2 business days); redeploy the workflow definition.

knownIssues.title: Parallel workflow branches rejoin prematurely before all approvers respond
knownIssues.content: The merge point is configured as 'ANY' instead of 'ALL', so the workflow continues as soon as any one approver completes. Solution: in Workflow Designer, select the merge step, and change the 'Required completions' property to 'All branches'; test with a multi-approver document before deploying to production.

knownIssues.title: Workflow launched via CE API sends step to wrong queue
knownIssues.content: The workflow launch API call is not specifying the correct work class, so the default routing rule is applying instead of the intended one. Solution: in the API call payload, explicitly set the WorkClass and Router properties; use the ICN Workflow Admin to verify that the correct default router is configured for the workflow definition.

knownIssues.title: Message flow fails to deploy: 'BIP2010E: The node type is not recognized'
knownIssues.content: The flow uses a node type (e.g., a database or MQ node) that requires a licensed feature that is not enabled on this ACE server. Solution: in the ACE admin console, check 'Server Administration > Product Overview' for enabled features; if the feature is licensed but not active, run 'mqsichangeproperties <broker> -c <execution group> -o ComIbmJMSProviderNode -n <nodeType>' to enable it.

knownIssues.title: ESQL compute node returns 'BIP3116E: An exception was thrown during evaluation'
knownIssues.content: An unhandled NULL reference or type mismatch in the ESQL logic is causing a runtime exception. Solution: add explicit NULL checks (IF EXISTS(InputRoot.JSON.Data.field[]) THEN) around all field references; enable message flow debugging in ACE toolkit and trace the message through the compute node to identify the failing path.

knownIssues.title: Message flow consuming from a file drops messages randomly
knownIssues.content: The File Input node is polling at an interval shorter than the time needed to process incoming files, causing the same file to be picked up twice before the lock is released. Solution: increase the polling interval in the File Input node properties; enable 'Keep file on completion' temporarily to diagnose; use an OS-level file lock (inode lease) before the file polling begins.

knownIssues.title: Flow runs in development but fails in production with 'BIP2230E: Could not find configurable service'
knownIssues.content: A configurable service (e.g., a JDBC provider or HTTP endpoint) defined in the development server is missing in production. Solution: export configurable services from the dev server using 'mqsilist <broker> -c' and import them to production via 'mqsicreateconfigurableservice'; use BAR override files to manage environment-specific values.

knownIssues.title: XML input validation fails for messages with Turkish characters (ISO-8859-9)
knownIssues.content: The XML parser defaults to UTF-8; if the incoming message does not declare the encoding in its XML prolog, Turkish characters are misread. Solution: add an ESQL compute node before the XML parsing step to set the message encoding: SET OutputRoot.Properties.Encoding = 1254; OR ensure the upstream system declares '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-9"?>' in the prolog.

knownIssues.title: HTTP Request node returns 'BIP3155E: Timeout waiting for response'
knownIssues.content: The default HTTP reply timeout (60 seconds) is exceeded by the downstream service. Solution: in the HTTP Request node properties, increase 'Request timeout' to match the expected service latency plus a buffer; for very slow services, consider an async request-reply pattern using a temporary reply queue.

knownIssues.title: Loopback between two flows causes a 'BIP2019E: Queue full' error
knownIssues.content: A message loop has formed because an error path or retry logic sends messages back to the same queue the flow reads from, without a finite retry limit. Solution: add a retry counter to the message properties (ESQL: SET OutputLocalEnvironment.Destination.MQ.DestinationData[1].replyToQ = 'DEAD.LETTER.QUEUE') and route to a dead-letter queue after N retries.

knownIssues.title: JDBC adapter returns 'CWBRE0043E: Connection pool exhausted'
knownIssues.content: All connections in the JDBC connection pool are in use, usually due to a slow query holding connections open. Solution: increase the JDBC configurable service 'maxConnections' property via 'mqsichangeproperties'; investigate the slow query using the database slow query log; ensure that ACE flow error handlers are closing database connections properly.

knownIssues.title: SAP adapter throws 'JCO_ERROR_COMMUNICATION: RFC_ERROR_COMM_FAILURE'
knownIssues.content: The SAP RFC connection lost its session due to an SAP system maintenance window or network interruption. Solution: configure connection retry in the SAP configurable service (maxRetries and retryDelay properties); implement a dead-letter queue pattern so messages are not lost during SAP outages.

knownIssues.title: Kafka connector produces messages but consumer flow never receives them
knownIssues.content: The consumer group ID in the ACE Kafka configurable service does not match the topic partition assignment. Solution: verify consumer group configuration via 'kafka-consumer-groups.sh --describe'; reset the consumer offset if needed with '--reset-offsets --to-earliest'; check that the topic name and Kafka broker list are identical in both producer and consumer configurations.

knownIssues.title: Email output node fails with 'BIP4218E: AuthenticationFailedException'
knownIssues.content: Modern Auth (OAuth 2.0) is required by the SMTP server, but the ACE Email node uses basic SMTP authentication. Solution: configure an SMTP relay (e.g., Postfix, mailpit in dev) that accepts basic auth on port 25 internally and relays via OAuth externally; update the SMTP configurable service to use the relay host.

knownIssues.title: FTP adapter connection drops after idle timeout
knownIssues.content: The FTP server closes connections that are idle for more than 5 minutes, but the ACE connection pool keeps the connections open longer. Solution: configure the FTP configurable service with a keepAlive interval shorter than the FTP server's idle timeout; or set maxConnections to 0 (no pooling) for infrequent FTP operations.

knownIssues.title: ACE operational log shows 'BIP2230E' but no messages in the error queue
knownIssues.content: The flow's catch terminal is not connected, so errors are logged but messages are silently discarded. Solution: always connect the catch terminal of every processing node to an explicit error handling sub-flow; the sub-flow should write to an error queue and create an audit record.

knownIssues.title: Message flow trace output overwhelms disk within minutes of enabling
knownIssues.content: ACE trace level 'normal' logs every node execution for every message, generating gigabytes quickly under load. Solution: use 'mqsichangeflowstats' to enable user trace only on specific nodes or specific correlation IDs; enable trace only during diagnostic windows, not in production continuously.

knownIssues.title: ACE dashboard shows flow as 'stopped' but it is still processing messages
knownIssues.content: The ACE admin agent has lost connectivity to the broker, but the broker process itself is running. Solution: restart the ACE admin agent via 'mqsistartadminagent'; verify the admin agent port (default 4414) is reachable; check for firewall changes that may have blocked the admin agent port.

knownIssues.title: Statistics service reports incorrect message counts for multi-instance flows
knownIssues.content: When a flow has multiple instances, the statistics service aggregates counts per instance but the dashboard displays per-execution-group totals. Solution: use the ACE REST API (/statistics endpoint) to query per-instance stats programmatically; or configure an MQ-based statistics destination that collects from all instances.

knownIssues.title: API publish fails: 'gateway service is not responding'
knownIssues.content: The DataPower Gateway is unreachable from the API Manager. Solution: verify network connectivity from the API Manager node to the DataPower gateway via 'curl https://gateway-host:3000/health'; check the gateway service registration in Cloud Manager > Infrastructure > Gateway Services; restart the DataPower domain if the health endpoint returns an error.

knownIssues.title: Swagger definition import fails with 'invalid OpenAPI specification'
knownIssues.content: The OpenAPI YAML or JSON contains an extension field or enum value not supported by API Connect's validator. Solution: validate the spec with 'ibm-openapi-validator swagger.yaml' CLI tool; common issues include '$ref' with external file paths (not supported in APIC), missing 'info.title', or 'operationId' values with special characters.

knownIssues.title: Published API appears in catalog but returns 404 from the gateway
knownIssues.content: The API endpoint path in the gateway does not match the base path defined in the OpenAPI spec. Solution: in API Manager, open the API > Host and Base Path settings and verify they match the gateway URL; re-publish the product to force the gateway to update its routing table.

knownIssues.title: API product version upgrade breaks existing subscriptions
knownIssues.content: When a new product version is published, existing app subscriptions are not automatically migrated to the new version. Solution: in API Manager > Products, use the 'Migrate subscriptions' wizard to move subscriptions from the old version to the new one before retiring the old product; communicate the migration plan to consuming teams in advance.

knownIssues.title: GraphQL API proxy returns 'introspection disabled' error
knownIssues.content: API Connect's default GraphQL security policy disables introspection in production catalogs. Solution: in the API definition, edit the GraphQL Introspection policy; if introspection is required for development tools, create a separate catalog with introspection enabled and restrict it by client ID.

knownIssues.title: OAuth token issued by APIC not accepted by backend service
knownIssues.content: The backend service is validating the JWT signature against a different JWK Set URL than the one APIC uses. Solution: in the backend service, configure the JWK Set URL to point to APIC's jwks endpoint (https://apic-gw-host/org/catalog/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/jwks); verify the 'iss' claim in the token matches the backend's expected issuer.

knownIssues.title: Client credentials flow returns 'invalid_client' for a valid application
knownIssues.content: The application's client secret has been rotated in APIC but the calling system still uses the old secret. Solution: in Consumer Manager, navigate to Apps > select app > Credentials and verify the current client secret; if the client secret was recently rotated, provide the new credentials to the consuming team.

knownIssues.title: JWT validation policy fails with 'token expired' although token is fresh
knownIssues.content: The DataPower gateway clock is out of sync with the authorization server clock by more than the 'clock skew' tolerance. Solution: synchronize DataPower NTP settings (configure terminal > clock timezone Europe/Istanbul; ntp server 10.0.0.1); increase the JWT policy's clock skew tolerance to 120 seconds as a short-term fix.

knownIssues.title: Mutual TLS (mTLS) API returns 403 even with correct client certificate
knownIssues.content: The DataPower gateway is not forwarding the client certificate to the API Connect security policy because TLS offload is configured incorrectly. Solution: in the DataPower multi-protocol gateway, enable 'Send Client Certificate' in the TLS client profile; in the API Connect policy, configure the certificate validation to use the forwarded header.

knownIssues.title: API key header is present but gateway returns 'unauthorized'
knownIssues.content: The API key security definition in the API spec specifies a header name with different case than what the calling application sends. Solution: HTTP headers are case-insensitive per RFC 7230, but the API Connect validation policy performs a case-sensitive match; align the header case in the API definition with the calling client.

knownIssues.title: Developer Portal shows blank page after upgrade
knownIssues.content: The Drupal theme or module used by the portal is incompatible with the upgraded API Connect version. Solution: after an APIC upgrade, always run 'apic portal:upgrade' to update the portal Drupal installation; clear the portal CDN cache and Drupal caches via 'drush cache-rebuild'.

knownIssues.title: API documentation on Developer Portal does not reflect latest changes
knownIssues.content: The portal content synchronization from the API Manager has failed silently. Solution: in Cloud Manager > Portal Services, trigger a manual sync from the portal service settings; check the portal service logs for synchronization errors; verify that the network path from API Manager to Portal is open on port 443.

knownIssues.title: Developer self-registration email not received
knownIssues.content: The portal's SMTP configuration is incorrect or the outbound email is being quarantined by the organization's spam filter. Solution: test SMTP connectivity from the portal server with 'telnet smtp-relay 25'; verify the FROM address is on the allowed senders list; check the mailpit/mail relay logs for delivery errors.

knownIssues.title: Application registration returns 'quota exceeded' on Developer Portal
knownIssues.content: The consumer organization has reached the maximum number of allowed applications defined in the billing plan. Solution: in Consumer Manager, increase the application quota for the consumer organization under Plans > Quota; or ask the developer to delete an unused application before creating a new one.

knownIssues.title: Queue manager fails to start with 'AMQ7017: Log not available'
knownIssues.content: The MQ log files are on a filesystem that has run out of space or the log path has changed. Solution: check available disk space with 'df -h' on the MQ log partition; if space is the issue, archive and remove old MQ logs from the error logs directory; verify the log path in the queue manager's qm.ini file matches the actual log location.

knownIssues.title: MQ Explorer cannot connect to remote queue manager
knownIssues.content: The MQ listener is not started, or the firewall blocks port 1414. Solution: start the listener with 'START LISTENER(SYSTEM.DEFAULT.LISTENER.TCP)' in the MQSC console; verify the port with 'DISPLAY LISTENER(*)'; add a firewall rule to allow TCP/1414 from the MQ Explorer host.

knownIssues.title: 'AMQ8135: Not authorized' when application tries to PUT to queue
knownIssues.content: The application's operating system user or MQ service account does not have 'put' authority on the target queue. Solution: grant authority using the MQSC command 'SET AUTHREC PROFILE(QUEUE.NAME) OBJTYPE(QUEUE) PRINCIPAL(svcuser) AUTHADD(PUT)'; verify with 'dspmqaut -m QMGR -n QUEUE.NAME -t queue -p svcuser'.

knownIssues.title: Queue manager keeps restarting in a crash loop
knownIssues.content: An error in the SYSTEM.DEAD.LETTER.QUEUE configuration or a persistent message with a corrupted header is causing the recovery process to fail. Solution: temporarily disable the dead-letter queue handler to allow the queue manager to start; use 'dmpmqmsg -m QMGR -i DLQ.DUMP.FILE' to inspect the DLQ; identify and remove the corrupted message.

knownIssues.title: Multi-instance queue manager fails to activate on the standby node
knownIssues.content: The shared filesystem where the queue manager data resides is not accessible from the standby server. Solution: verify NFS/CIFS mount availability from the standby server with 'mount -v'; check that the MQ user ID has consistent UID/GID on both nodes; verify that no file locks are left by the failed primary using 'lsof' on the shared path.

knownIssues.title: Sender channel stuck in 'RETRYING' state
knownIssues.content: The receiving queue manager is down or the network is intermittent. Solution: check the receiver queue manager status; use 'PING CHANNEL(CHANNEL.NAME)' from MQSC to test connectivity; if the issue is persistent, check the channel error log under /var/mqm/qmgrs/QMNAME/errors/AMQERR01.LOG for the specific error code.

knownIssues.title: Channel MCAUSER mismatch causes AMQ9557 'Channel partner not authorized'
knownIssues.content: The MCAUSER on the receiving channel does not match the user specified by the sending channel. Solution: align the MCAUSER on the receiver channel definition with the user that the sender is presenting; or use an MQ channel authentication record (CHLAUTH) to map the sending user to a local user: 'SET CHLAUTH(CHANNEL.NAME) TYPE(USERMAP) CLNTUSER(sender) MCAUSER(mquser)'.

knownIssues.title: Message batches arrive out of order on the receiving queue
knownIssues.content: Multiple sender channels are running in parallel to the same queue, and network latency differences cause re-ordering. Solution: reduce the number of parallel instances to 1 for queues requiring strict ordering; or use the MQMD sequence number in the consuming application to reorder messages if parallel channels are required for throughput.

knownIssues.title: SSL/TLS channel fails with 'AMQ9641: Remote CipherSpec did not match'
knownIssues.content: The cipher specification configured on the sender and receiver channels are different. Solution: align the CipherSpec on both ends using a strong spec: 'ALTER CHANNEL(CHANNEL.NAME) CHLTYPE(SDR) SSLCIPH(TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA256)'; if the cipher mismatch is between an old and new MQ version, check IBM compatibility notes for that cipher.

knownIssues.title: High number of uncommitted messages on channel causes MAXUNCOMMITTEDMSGS error
knownIssues.content: The consuming application is processing messages in large transactions without committing frequently enough. Solution: reduce the batch size in the consuming application to commit every N messages (typically 100-500); adjust the MAXUNCOMMITTEDMSGS channel attribute to match the expected transaction size.

knownIssues.title: Messages land on the dead-letter queue with reason MQRC_NOT_AUTHORIZED
knownIssues.content: The DLQ handler is re-routing messages to a target queue where the service account does not have PUT authority. Solution: review the DLQ handler rules file (SYSTEM.DEAD.LETTER.QUEUE.RULES.txt); grant PUT authority on all queues referenced in DLQ handler rules; use 'dspmqaut' to verify current authorities before applying changes.

knownIssues.title: Message expiry is not working - expired messages remain on the queue
knownIssues.content: The queue or the queue manager has 'NORETRIEVE' set, which prevents expired message removal on GET. Solution: set 'MSGDLVSQ(PRIORITY)' and 'NPMCLASS(NORMAL)' on the queue; verify that consuming applications call MQGET with 'MQGMO_ACCEPT_TRUNCATED_MSG' so the MQ expiry mechanism can run; expired messages are only removed when a GET is attempted.

knownIssues.title: Large messages (>100MB) cause channel to stall
knownIssues.content: The channel's MAXMSGL attribute is set lower than the message size. Solution: increase MAXMSGL on both sender and receiver channels: 'ALTER CHANNEL(NAME) CHLTYPE(SDR) MAXMSGL(104857600)'; also increase the queue's MAXMSGL and the queue manager's MAXMSGL attribute to match.

knownIssues.title: Published form does not appear on the mobile device after sync
knownIssues.content: The form was published to a different user group than the one the device belongs to. Solution: in Inviso Admin Portal, navigate to Forms > Edit Form > Assignments and verify that the correct user group or specific users are assigned; trigger a manual sync from the device (Settings > Sync) after correcting the assignment.

knownIssues.title: Conditional logic on a form field does not trigger on iOS but works on Android
knownIssues.content: The JavaScript expression used in the conditional rule contains a method not supported by the iOS WebView engine version. Solution: replace arrow functions and template literals in condition expressions with ES5-compatible syntax; test conditional logic on the lowest supported iOS version before publishing.

knownIssues.title: Calculated field shows incorrect result after editing a dependent field
knownIssues.content: The calculation formula references the field's 'saved value' instead of the 'current value'. Solution: in the form designer, open the calculated field's formula settings and ensure the referenced fields use 'real-time' binding; republish the form after correcting the formula.

knownIssues.title: Dropdown list in form not loading from the master data API
knownIssues.content: The API endpoint providing the dropdown values is returning a CORS error or a 401 Unauthorized because the device cannot reach the server. Solution: verify the master data API URL is accessible from the mobile network (not just corporate Wi-Fi); ensure the API key or token used by Inviso is current and has not expired.

knownIssues.title: Form with photo attachment field freezes when multiple photos are selected
knownIssues.content: Selecting more than 3 high-resolution photos simultaneously overwhelms the device memory available to the form renderer. Solution: set a maximum of 2 attachments per photo field in the form designer; advise users to resize photos to medium quality before attaching; consider adding a server-side compression step.

knownIssues.title: Inviso mobile app crashes on startup after an OS update
knownIssues.content: An OS update changed the WebView version, causing a compatibility issue with the app's internal rendering engine. Solution: check the Inviso release notes for the compatible OS version range; update the Inviso mobile app to the latest version via the app store; if a compatible version is not yet available, roll back the OS update on the affected device.

knownIssues.title: Completed forms are not syncing from mobile to server
knownIssues.content: The device has lost connectivity to the Inviso server and submissions are queued locally. Solution: verify server connectivity from the device by opening the Inviso server URL in the device browser; check that the device date/time is correct (certificate validation fails if the clock is wrong); force sync from Settings > Sync Now.

knownIssues.title: Offline form data is lost when the app is force-closed
knownIssues.content: The local database was not committed before the app was terminated. Solution: Inviso uses SQLite for offline storage; the app auto-saves form data every 30 seconds, but a forced kill can lose the last unsaved window. Advise users to use the form's 'Save Draft' button before closing; do not force-close the app during active data entry.

knownIssues.title: GPS coordinates in form submission are inaccurate (off by 500+ meters)
knownIssues.content: The device acquired a cached GPS fix from a previous location. Solution: in the form's location field settings, enable 'Force fresh GPS reading'; instruct users to allow a few seconds for the GPS icon to turn green (indicating a fresh fix) before submitting location data.

knownIssues.title: Form submission data not appearing in the Inviso dashboard report
knownIssues.content: The report filter is set to a specific date range that excludes the recent submissions. Solution: in the Inviso Admin Portal > Reports, reset the date filter to 'All time' or the correct date range; verify that the submissions were actually sent by checking the device's sync log.

knownIssues.title: CSV export from Inviso includes extra columns not in the form
knownIssues.content: The export template was not updated after the form was modified to remove fields. Solution: regenerate the export template in Reports > Export Settings to match the current form version; note that previous submissions with the old structure will still export the old columns.

knownIssues.title: Inviso API for reading submissions returns 429 Too Many Requests
knownIssues.content: The integration is polling the submission API too frequently. Solution: implement exponential back-off in the polling client; use Inviso webhooks instead of polling to receive real-time submission notifications; contact Inviso support to increase the rate limit for the organization if higher throughput is required.

knownIssues.title: New Inviso user sees 'No forms available' after account creation
knownIssues.content: The user account is in 'Pending Activation' state because the activation email link was not clicked. Solution: ask the user to check their spam folder for the Inviso activation email; an administrator can also manually activate the account from Inviso Admin Portal > Users > select user > Activate Account.

knownIssues.title: Inviso server response time increases as submission table grows
knownIssues.content: The submissions table has grown to millions of rows without indexes on the commonly queried columns. Solution: add a composite database index on (form_id, status, created_at); configure Inviso's archive/purge setting to move submissions older than 12 months to the archive table to keep the active table small.

knownIssues.title: Inviso Admin Portal login returns 'User not found' for a valid AD account
knownIssues.content: The LDAP/AD search base in Inviso is restricted to a specific OU that does not include the user's OU. Solution: in Inviso Admin > System Settings > Authentication, expand the LDAP search base to the domain root (DC=company,DC=com) or add the user's OU to the search base; test with the LDAP query tool before saving.

knownIssues.title: Uploaded receipt returns 'Could not extract total amount'
knownIssues.content: The receipt image is blurry or taken at an angle, preventing OCR from reliably reading the total. Solution: retake the photo in good lighting, holding the camera parallel to the receipt surface; FiGO's OCR works best when the receipt is flat and the image is at least 300 DPI; the user can also manually enter the amount if OCR fails.

knownIssues.title: FiGO assigns wrong expense category to restaurant receipts
knownIssues.content: The AI classification model has not been fine-tuned on the organization's merchant category mapping. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Expense Categories > Classification Rules, add a rule that maps the detected merchant name or category code to the correct internal expense type; over time, user corrections will improve the model.

knownIssues.title: Foreign currency receipt total is converted at an incorrect exchange rate
knownIssues.content: FiGO uses the exchange rate at the time of document upload, not the transaction date. Solution: in FiGO Settings > Currency Settings, enable 'Use transaction date for exchange rate'; the user can also manually override the exchange rate on the expense item.

knownIssues.title: Invoice uploaded as PDF returns blank extraction results
knownIssues.content: The PDF is image-based (scanned) rather than text-based, and the PDF OCR pipeline is disabled. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Document Processing, enable 'OCR for scanned PDFs'; note that image-based PDF OCR is slower and less accurate than text-based extraction; encourage suppliers to send native digital invoices.

knownIssues.title: Duplicate receipt detection is not triggering for identical receipts uploaded by two users
knownIssues.content: The duplicate detection algorithm compares receipts within the same user account, not across users. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Policies > Duplicate Detection, enable 'Cross-user duplicate check' for the expense policy; this will flag receipts with identical total, date, and merchant across all users in the organization.

knownIssues.title: Receipt with split VAT rates (8% and 18%) is extracted as a single total VAT
knownIssues.content: FiGO's default extraction model extracts a single VAT field; it does not split multi-rate VAT without a custom field mapping. Solution: add custom extraction fields in FiGO Admin > Field Mapping for 'VAT_8' and 'VAT_18'; use the regex-based extraction rule targeting the specific line items on Turkish receipts.

knownIssues.title: Expense report submitted but not appearing in manager's approval queue
knownIssues.content: The approval routing rule is based on the employee's cost center, which is not populated in the FiGO user profile. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Users, verify that each user's cost center and reporting manager fields are correctly filled; expense reports route based on these fields.

knownIssues.title: Approver receives 'already processed' error when clicking the approval email link
knownIssues.content: Another approver in a parallel approval flow (or the same approver from a different device) already acted on the request. Solution: FiGO sends approval links to all approvers simultaneously; the first approval locks the request. Redesign the workflow to use sequential approval if concurrent approvals cause confusion.

knownIssues.title: Expense policy violation warning not shown to user before submission
knownIssues.content: The policy rule is set to 'enforce' mode instead of 'warn' mode, causing silent rejection instead of displaying a warning. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Policies, change the violation action from 'Reject' to 'Warn and require justification'; this allows users to acknowledge the violation and provide a business reason.

knownIssues.title: Approved expenses not flowing to ERP system for payment
knownIssues.content: The FiGO-to-ERP integration webhook is failing with a certificate error due to a recent ERP SSL certificate renewal. Solution: update the SSL certificate in FiGO Admin > Integrations > ERP Connection; test the connection and verify that the ERP endpoint is reachable from the FiGO server.

knownIssues.title: Expense report reimbursement amount differs from what the user submitted
knownIssues.content: A policy cap (e.g., daily meal allowance limit) was applied during processing, reducing the reimbursable amount. Solution: in FiGO, the policy cap application is shown in the expense detail view under 'Policy adjustments'; add a notification step in the approval workflow that informs the employee when a cap has been applied.

knownIssues.title: FiGO expense export to Logo ERP returns 'Invalid account code'
knownIssues.content: The expense categories in FiGO are not mapped to the correct Logo ERP account codes. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Integrations > Logo ERP > Account Mapping, create a mapping entry for each expense category to the corresponding Logo chart of accounts code; test the mapping with a single export before running bulk exports.

knownIssues.title: Exported invoices in FiGO are missing e-Invoice UBL fields
knownIssues.content: The Turkish e-Invoice (e-Fatura) integration requires specific UBL fields that are not mapped in the default FiGO export template. Solution: customize the FiGO e-Fatura export template in Admin > Integrations > e-Fatura to include supplier VKN, invoice scenario (TICARIFATURA/EARSIVFATURA), and the GIB integration provider API credentials.

knownIssues.title: Duplicate invoice entries in ERP after FiGO sync
knownIssues.content: The FiGO-to-ERP sync job ran twice due to a network timeout that did not receive a success response on the first attempt. Solution: implement idempotency in the ERP integration by checking for existing invoice reference numbers before inserting; use FiGO's built-in 'Mark as exported' flag to prevent re-exporting already-synced records.

knownIssues.title: FiGO mobile app asks for login every time it opens
knownIssues.content: The app's session token TTL is very short, or the device's secure keychain is clearing credentials on app backgrounding. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Security Settings, increase the mobile session timeout to 8 hours; on iOS, verify that the app has Keychain Sharing enabled in entitlements; on Android, verify the AccountManager credential storage is not being cleared by the device's battery optimization.

knownIssues.title: Camera in FiGO mobile app does not launch on Android 14
knownIssues.content: Android 14 introduced stricter media permissions; the app requires the new granular media permissions that replaced the broad READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE permission. Solution: update FiGO mobile app to the latest version that targets Android 14 and requests READ_MEDIA_IMAGES and CAMERA permissions separately.

knownIssues.title: Submitted expense report shows 'pending' status for more than 24 hours
knownIssues.content: The approver's email notification bounced or was filtered as spam, and the approver is unaware of the pending item. Solution: in FiGO Admin > Notifications, enable 'Pending approval reminder' emails at 24-hour intervals; also check the approver's spam folder for FiGO notification emails.

knownIssues.title: Instana agent installed but no data appears in the Instana UI
knownIssues.content: The agent cannot reach the Instana backend because port 443 (or the configured backend port) is blocked by the corporate firewall. Solution: verify connectivity from the agent host with 'curl -v https://<backend-host>:443/healthz'; open the required ports in the firewall; also check that the agent key in agent.cfg is correct.

knownIssues.title: Java application not detected by Instana agent auto-instrumentation
knownIssues.content: The JVM startup arguments do not include the Instana Java agent javaagent flag, or the application is starting before the agent is fully initialized. Solution: add '-javaagent:/opt/instana/agent/lib/instana-javaagent.jar' to the JVM startup arguments; verify the agent log at /opt/instana/agent/data/log/agent.log for auto-discovery events.

knownIssues.title: Instana agent consuming excessive CPU (>30%) on the host
knownIssues.content: A high-traffic application with many spans is causing the agent's tracer to buffer and process large volumes of telemetry. Solution: in agent.cfg, reduce 'com.instana.agent.main.tracer.sampling.rate' to sample at 50% instead of 100%; set 'com.instana.agent.main.tracer.span.max.queue.size' to limit memory usage; contact Instana support for workload-specific tuning.

knownIssues.title: Kubernetes Instana agent DaemonSet pods stuck in CrashLoopBackOff
knownIssues.content: The agent image is trying to access node-level host paths that are restricted by the Kubernetes pod security policy. Solution: create a ClusterRole that grants the agent the required host volume and privileged container permissions; apply the Instana-provided RBAC manifest from the official installation documentation.

knownIssues.title: Alert rule triggers on every deployment even though it should be suppressed
knownIssues.content: The maintenance window or deployment marker is not linked to the alert rule's suppression settings. Solution: in Instana, navigate to Settings > Alerting > Alert Channels, and under the specific rule, configure a deployment window suppression; ensure the CI/CD pipeline sends a change marker to Instana via the API before and after deployment.

knownIssues.title: Email alert not received even though alert fired in Instana UI
knownIssues.content: The alert channel email configuration is pointing to an invalid SMTP relay or a group email that has exceeded its inbox quota. Solution: in Settings > Alerting > Alert Channels > Email, test the channel using the 'Send Test Message' button and review the delivery result; verify the SMTP relay logs.

knownIssues.title: Threshold-based alert fires on every 60-second check interval with no actual issue
knownIssues.content: The threshold is set below the normal baseline of the monitored metric. Solution: analyze the metric's historical data in Instana to determine the normal operating range; set the threshold at mean + 2 standard deviations; use a 'consecutive breaches' condition (e.g., breach for 5 consecutive minutes) instead of a single-point trigger.

knownIssues.title: PagerDuty integration receives alert but with missing application context
knownIssues.content: The Instana alert payload is not including the 'service' and 'application perspective' context that PagerDuty uses for routing. Solution: in the Instana alert channel settings for PagerDuty, configure the custom payload template to include '{{event.entity.label}}' and '{{event.application.name}}'; test the payload with a manual alert trigger.

knownIssues.title: Traces are incomplete - only the first service hop is visible
knownIssues.content: The downstream services are not propagating the Instana trace context headers (X-INSTANA-T and X-INSTANA-S). Solution: verify that all services in the call chain have the Instana agent and tracer installed; for services using non-standard HTTP clients, manually inject the W3C Trace Context headers.

knownIssues.title: Database call latency in traces shows 0ms for all PostgreSQL queries
knownIssues.content: The Instana agent is not recognizing the PostgreSQL JDBC driver version being used. Solution: check the Instana agent log for 'database sensor initialization' messages; update the PostgreSQL JDBC driver to a version supported by the Instana sensor list; the Instana PostgreSQL sensor supports drivers 9.4+.

knownIssues.title: Service dependency map shows duplicate service nodes
knownIssues.content: Two instances of the same service are running with different 'service.name' configuration values in their Instana agent settings. Solution: standardize the 'com.instana.agent.main.services.name' property across all instances of the service; the value must be identical for Instana to group them as one logical service.

knownIssues.title: Datacap scanner client cannot detect the Fujitsu scanner
knownIssues.content: The scanner driver is not installed on the scanning workstation, or the ISIS driver version is incompatible. Solution: install the Fujitsu ISIS driver version specified in the Datacap compatibility matrix; set the scanner source in Datacap Scan > Scanner Settings to 'ISIS' and select the Fujitsu model; restart the Datacap application after driver installation.

knownIssues.title: Scanned documents are arriving with skewed pages
knownIssues.content: The scanner's automatic deskew feature is disabled or not supported for the selected scan resolution. Solution: enable 'Deskew' in the scanner profile settings in Datacap Admin; if the scanner does not support hardware deskew, enable Datacap's software deskew action in the batch class workflow.

knownIssues.title: Batch import via hot folder is not picking up PDFs
knownIssues.content: The hot folder monitor service is looking for TIFF files only, as specified in the batch class import settings. Solution: in Datacap Navigator > Batch Class > Import, add 'pdf' to the accepted file extensions; also verify that the Datacap service account has read/write access to the hot folder path.

knownIssues.title: 'Batch is locked by another user' error prevents processing
knownIssues.content: A previous user's session crashed while processing the batch, leaving a lock record in the Datacap database. Solution: in Datacap Navigator as an administrator, navigate to the locked batch, right-click and select 'Unlock batch'; if the batch is still corrupted, use 'Reset batch' to return it to the beginning of the workflow.

knownIssues.title: OCR recognition rate drops below 70% for handwritten forms
knownIssues.content: Datacap's default Kofax OCR engine is optimized for printed text, not handwriting. Solution: enable the ICR (Intelligent Character Recognition) engine in the Datacap zone OCR action settings; for critical fields with low accuracy, configure a manual verification step in the workflow; alternatively, evaluate FiGO or Watson for handwriting.

knownIssues.title: Field extraction returns correct value in test but fails in production
knownIssues.content: The production batch class is using a different OCR profile than the development environment. Solution: export the exact OCR profile and field extraction rules from the test environment using Datacap's batch class export; import and activate it in production; verify that the document layouts are consistent between environments.

knownIssues.title: Turkish characters (s, i, o, u with diacritics) are misrecognized as Latin equivalents
knownIssues.content: The OCR engine language is set to English instead of Turkish. Solution: in the Datacap OCR action properties, set the 'Language' to 'Turkish'; if Kofax OCR does not include Turkish, install the Turkish language pack or switch to the ABBYY FineReader OCR engine which has robust Turkish support.

knownIssues.title: Table extraction from invoices captures incorrect row data
knownIssues.content: The table extraction zone is defined with fixed coordinates that shift for invoices from different suppliers with varying table layouts. Solution: use Datacap's 'Learn' mode to train the extraction model on a representative sample of each supplier's invoice; enable 'Flexible table extraction' to allow for variable row heights and column positions.

knownIssues.title: Datacap action fails with 'RuleSet not found' after batch class import
knownIssues.content: The ruleset file referenced in the batch class was not included in the export package. Solution: when exporting a batch class, ensure 'Include custom actions and rulesets' is checked; manually copy the missing .rls ruleset files to the Datacap server's RuleManager directory and reload the batch class.

knownIssues.title: Validation action marks correct data as invalid
knownIssues.content: The validation regular expression or lookup table has an error that is excluding valid values. Solution: test the validation rule using the Datacap RuleManager 'Test' function with known-good sample values; for regex rules, use an online Turkish regex tester to verify patterns for Turkish ID numbers (TC Kimlik), tax numbers, and dates.

knownIssues.title: Export to FileNet action fails with 'Document class not found'
knownIssues.content: The document class mapping in the Datacap export action references a class name that has been renamed or does not exist in the target FileNet Object Store. Solution: in Datacap Navigator > Batch Class > Export > FileNet settings, update the document class mapping to match the current FileNet class names; use ACCE to verify the exact class name including case.

knownIssues.title: Datacap nightly batch fails with OutOfMemoryError on large document sets
knownIssues.content: Multi-page documents accumulate in the Rulerunner JVM heap during a large batch run. Solution: increase the Rulerunner JVM heap in the startup script (e.g., -Xmx3g); configure the batch class to use a maximum batch size (e.g., 500 documents per run) so memory is released between segments.

knownIssues.title: Batch processing pauses at every document waiting for operator confirmation
knownIssues.content: The verification step in the batch class is set to 'Manual verification required' instead of automatic mode. Solution: in Datacap Navigator > Batch Class > Verification action, change the mode to 'Automatic - skip if confidence above threshold' (recommended 80%); documents below the threshold will still require manual review.

knownIssues.title: Scheduled batch job does not start at the configured time
knownIssues.content: The Datacap Task Server service is not running or the scheduled job trigger has been disabled. Solution: verify the Datacap Task Server service is running in Windows Services; in Datacap Navigator > Scheduled Jobs, confirm the job is enabled and the trigger time is correct; check the Task Server log for errors.

knownIssues.title: Datacap export to FileNet fails after Content Engine upgrade
knownIssues.content: A Content Engine upgrade may change the connection protocol (HTTP to HTTPS) or endpoint URL. Solution: in Datacap Navigator > Batch Class > Export > FileNet Connector, update the Content Engine URL to the new protocol and port; if HTTPS is now required, ensure the Datacap server trusts the FileNet SSL certificate by importing it into the Java truststore.

knownIssues.title: Datacap output files written to wrong location after server reconfiguration
knownIssues.content: The export path uses a mapped drive letter that was changed or lost after a server reboot. Solution: change the export path from the drive letter (e.g., F:\\output) to the UNC path (e.g., \\\\fileserver\\datacap\\output); UNC paths are resolved at the system level and are not affected by user session drive mappings.

knownIssues.title: Datacap CMIS export fails with 'Authentication required' to external system
knownIssues.content: The CMIS repository credentials stored in the Datacap export action have expired or been rotated. Solution: in Datacap Navigator > Batch Class > Export > CMIS action, update the username and password for the target CMIS repository; test the connection from the action properties before saving; consider using a dedicated service account with a non-expiring password.

knownIssues.title: Datacap license error when registering a new scanning workstation
knownIssues.content: The Datacap license has reached its maximum registered workstation or concurrent user limit. Solution: in Datacap Administration > License Manager, review the registered workstations and deactivate any that are no longer in use; if the license limit is insufficient, contact 32bit to obtain additional workstation seats.

knownIssues.title: Datacap services do not start automatically after server reboot
knownIssues.content: The Datacap Application Server and Task Server services are set to 'Manual' startup type. Solution: in Windows Services (services.msc), set all Datacap services to 'Automatic (Delayed Start)'; verify that the service account password has not expired; check the Windows Event Log under Application for service start failure details.

knownIssues.title: Unauthorized configuration changes made by a low-privilege user
knownIssues.content: A user with Datacap Operator role was inadvertently granted Administrator role, allowing them to modify batch class configurations. Solution: in Datacap Administration > Users, review all role assignments and correct any over-privileged accounts; Operator role should be used for running batches only; Administrator role should be restricted to designated IT staff.

knownIssues.title: Market Data Integrator shows 'feed disconnected' for Bloomberg data source
knownIssues.content: The Bloomberg B-PIPE session has expired or the Bloomberg license has not been renewed. Solution: verify the Bloomberg SAPI/B-PIPE connection status on the Bloomberg terminal with 'CONN <GO>'; check the Bloomberg license expiry with the Bloomberg account manager; restart the B-PIPE session from the MDI admin console.

knownIssues.title: Rate Distribution Engine pushing stale prices to downstream systems
knownIssues.content: The RDE cache invalidation interval is set too high, causing it to serve cached prices after a market-moving event. Solution: in RDE admin settings, reduce the cache TTL to 1 second for real-time price feeds; configure 'forced refresh on price change exceeding X%' to bypass caching on large moves.

knownIssues.title: FX spot rates show a 3-5 pip spread inconsistency between two distribution channels
knownIssues.content: Two distribution channels are pulling rates from different MDI connections with slightly different latency and rounding settings. Solution: normalize all downstream channels to use the same MDI endpoint; align the rounding precision setting (pip definition) across all rate distribution channels to the same decimal places.

knownIssues.title: Historical data gaps in the Financial Data Integrator for non-business days
knownIssues.content: The holiday calendar used by FDI for data gap detection does not include Turkish public holidays. Solution: in FDI admin, import the Turkish public holiday calendar (Borsa Istanbul official calendar) under Settings > Holiday Calendars; set the FDI calendar for each instrument group to 'Turkey (BIST)'.

knownIssues.title: Marketwatch dashboard does not refresh prices during the last 30 minutes of trading
knownIssues.content: A scheduled cleanup job runs at 17:30 and locks the price cache table, blocking real-time price updates. Solution: reschedule the cleanup job to run outside trading hours (e.g., 08:00 AM); use a non-locking 'truncate' operation instead of a row-by-row 'delete' to minimize lock duration.

knownIssues.title: FX Platform order rejected with 'counterparty limit exceeded'
knownIssues.content: The netting position with the selected counterparty has reached its configured credit limit. Solution: in FX Platform Admin > Counterparty Management, review the current net exposure versus the limit; either reduce the position with the counterparty or request a temporary limit increase with the risk team's approval.

knownIssues.title: Transaction execution time exceeds SLA (>200ms) during peak trading
knownIssues.content: The order routing engine is queueing orders because the price engine CPU is saturated by concurrent market data updates. Solution: scale the price engine horizontally by adding a second instance; configure order routing to load balance between instances; review the order execution queue depth during peak hours using the FX Platform monitoring dashboard.

knownIssues.title: MetaTrader Integrator fails to acknowledge trade confirmations
knownIssues.content: The MT4/MT5 trade confirmation protocol expects an ACK within 500ms, but network latency between the FX Platform and MT server is 600ms. Solution: co-locate the FintechBox FX Platform and the MetaTrader server in the same data center or on the same VLAN to reduce latency below 100ms; configure the MT bridge to increase the ACK timeout.

knownIssues.title: Currency pair settlement dates are calculated incorrectly around month-end
knownIssues.content: The FX Platform's settlement date calculator does not account for the Borsa Istanbul settlement calendar at month boundaries. Solution: update the settlement date calendar in FX Platform Admin > Settlement Calendars > BIST; verify that the 'end-of-month convention' is set to 'Modified Following' for TRY pairs.

knownIssues.title: FintechBox user cannot access real-time feeds after role change
knownIssues.content: The user's entitlement cache on the FintechBox licensing server has not been refreshed after the role change in the admin portal. Solution: in FintechBox Admin > Users, force a cache refresh for the specific user; it can also be triggered by logging out and back in; the full refresh cycle runs automatically every 15 minutes.

knownIssues.title: 'Concurrent user limit reached' error blocks new logins
knownIssues.content: All licensed concurrent user slots are occupied. Solution: in FintechBox Admin > License Management, view active sessions; an admin can forcefully terminate idle sessions to free up slots; contact the 32bit account manager to expand the concurrent user license if this is a recurring issue.

knownIssues.title: API key for FintechBox integration expired but no expiry notification was sent
knownIssues.content: The API key notification email was sent to a former employee's address that is now bouncing. Solution: immediately generate a new API key from FintechBox Admin > API Keys; update the integration configuration on the consuming system; change the notification email for API key expiry to a shared IT mailbox.

knownIssues.title: Bot fails on 'Object Not Found' when targeting a UI element
knownIssues.content: The target application's UI element ID or XPath has changed after an application update. Solution: in Automation Anywhere Bot Creator, open the task and use 'Capture' to re-record the failing UI element; prefer object identification by 'Name' or 'AutomationId' attributes over screen coordinates for more resilient automation.

knownIssues.title: AA bot works in development but fails in production with 'Application not found'
knownIssues.content: The target application path is hardcoded in the bot to a developer machine path that does not exist on the production bot runner. Solution: parameterize all file paths using Automation Anywhere global variables or credential vault entries; use relative paths instead of absolute paths; verify the application is installed on the bot runner VM.

knownIssues.title: Excel automation bot throws 'Excel not responding' after processing 5000+ rows
knownIssues.content: The Excel application is running out of memory because the bot is not closing and releasing the Excel COM object between batches. Solution: add an 'Excel > Close Spreadsheet' action at the end of each batch iteration; enable 'Excel Automation > Enable Background Mode' to prevent Excel UI from rendering during processing.

knownIssues.title: Bot incorrectly reads decimal values from a web table (Turkish locale)
knownIssues.content: The bot is running in a Windows session with English locale, so Turkish decimal separators (comma) are read as thousand separators. Solution: either set the bot runner VM locale to Turkish (tr-TR) in Regional Settings; or add an ESQL/string manipulation step to convert Turkish-format numbers (1.234,56 to 1234.56) before processing.

knownIssues.title: Bot scheduled in Control Room does not run at the configured time
knownIssues.content: The Control Room server and the bot runner VM are in different time zones, causing a scheduling offset. Solution: ensure both Control Room and all bot runner VMs are configured to the same timezone (Europe/Istanbul); in Control Room > Schedules, verify the displayed 'Next run time' shows the correct local time.

knownIssues.title: Bot deployment from Control Room fails: 'Bot runner not available'
knownIssues.content: The Automation Anywhere agent service on the bot runner VM has stopped. Solution: connect to the bot runner VM and restart the 'Automation Anywhere Agent' Windows service; if the service fails to start, check the agent log at %ProgramData%\AutomationAnywhere\BotAgent\Logs\; verify that the bot runner VM network can reach the Control Room on port 443.

knownIssues.title: Running bot is terminated unexpectedly and marked as 'Failed' in Control Room
knownIssues.content: The bot runner VM triggered an OS-level screen saver or sleep state, interrupting the running session. Solution: configure the bot runner VM's power settings to 'High performance' with screen saver disabled; set the Windows session timeout to 'Never'; configure the bot runner as a dedicated account that never auto-locks.

knownIssues.title: Budget period cannot be created for the new fiscal year
knownIssues.content: The previous fiscal year's budget has not been closed out, and the portal does not allow overlapping active periods. Solution: navigate to Finance Portal > Budget Management > Periods and set the current year's status to 'Closed'; then create the new fiscal year period with the correct start and end dates.

knownIssues.title: Department budget variance report shows incorrect actuals
knownIssues.content: The actuals are being pulled from a cache that has not been synchronized with the latest approved invoices from the payment system. Solution: trigger a manual data sync from Finance Portal > Admin > Data Sync > ERP Sync Now; verify the sync log for errors; schedule the sync to run every 2 hours during business hours.

knownIssues.title: Budget transfer between cost centers is not reflected in the portal
knownIssues.content: Budget transfers entered directly in the ERP system bypass the Finance Portal's approval workflow and are not picked up by the integration. Solution: route all budget transfers through the Finance Portal's transfer request workflow to ensure they are tracked; if ad-hoc ERP transfers must be allowed, add a reconciliation job that imports ERP transfers nightly.

knownIssues.title: Budget utilization percentage exceeds 100% with no warning triggered
knownIssues.content: The budget alert threshold is set to 110% instead of 90% or 100%, delaying the notification. Solution: in Finance Portal > Budget Settings > Alerts, lower the utilization alert threshold to 85% for an early warning and 100% for a critical alert; assign the alerts to both the budget owner and their manager.

knownIssues.title: Vendor invoice stuck in 'Pending Approval' for more than 5 business days
knownIssues.content: The assigned approver is on leave and there is no delegation configured in the Finance Portal. Solution: in Finance Portal > User Management, configure 'Approval Delegation' so that when the primary approver is absent, approvals route to a designated backup; as an immediate fix, an admin can reassign the pending invoice from the admin queue.

knownIssues.title: Recurring payment fails because the vendor bank account details have changed
knownIssues.content: The vendor updated their IBAN in the Finance Portal but the payment was already queued with the old IBAN.
